derivation: Two measurements, read off their run records under $THRULINE_PILOT_SP/pilot. (a) The stratified 10-task oracle probe, run-id prefix `probe-p1-`. (b) The 123-task scripted-agent measurement, run-id prefix `m1-`, which is the one the 64/99 chain-coverage figure came from. Per task the sources are: `mount-<rid>/READY`, `mount-<rid>/spool`, `mount-<rid>/exec.db`, `mount-<rid>/hook-install.log`, `mount-<rid>/task-provenance.txt`, `receipts-<rid>/<task>.json` (+ its `.stdout`), `staged-<rid>/<task>/Dockerfile`, `staged-<rid>/.thruline-layer`, and `runs-<rid>/<rid>/run.log` + `results.json`. Paths are recorded relative to that pilot directory on purpose: an absolute path here would carry one machine's home into a committed file.
why_this_file_exists: A task the instrument breaks produces an EMPTY spool. Folded into an average whose denominator still counts it, an empty spool contributes a ZERO, and the metric then reports the instrument's own damage as the product under-performing (BUILD-SPEC §12, §20.3, operator Ruling 6). The empty-spool signature is NOT self-explaining: `spring-messaging-vul` below has a byte-for-byte identical signature to two instrument failures and is neither the instrument's fault nor ThruLine's. That is why this is a file a human writes and the report READS, not a heuristic the report guesses.
why_v2: v1 could be satisfied by a file that exists. It had no `attestations` (so an empty `entries` list was indistinguishable from a set nobody read against the run being reported), no `applies_to` (so a mechanism measured in one run silently classified every other run naming that task), and no `evidence_tier` (so an argued mechanism read exactly like a reproduced one). All three were live defects: the published 64/99 figure bypassed this file entirely, and of the m1 measurement's 24 exclusions v1 classified 3.

classes.instrument: ThruLine's own instrumentation BROKE the task. EXCLUDED from every coverage denominator; counted and named separately as `instrument_failures`.
classes.ceiling: ThruLine's own instrumentation REFUSED the task and said so, non-zero, before anything ran. Not damage and not a product result — the doctrine's ceiling (`a task the instrument cannot reach`, PILOT-REPORT.md vocabulary note). EXCLUDED and named.
classes.environment: Something outside both ThruLine and the task broke it (a busy host port, host DNS, a read timeout on a package index). EXCLUDED from every coverage denominator, reported under its own heading. Not an instrument failure and not a product result.
classes.task-upstream: The task's own image or setup no longer builds, on its own terms, independent of ThruLine and of this host — a pinned upstream that changed under it. EXCLUDED and named. Kept apart from `environment` because calling it environmental would assert something false about where the defect lives.
classes.run-incomplete: The run did not finish: no `results.json`, and the record ends mid-flight. There is no outcome to attribute to anyone. EXCLUDED and named, because a run nobody finished is not a zero and is not a pass.
classes.product: The capture is empty and that IS a ThruLine result. COUNTED in the denominator as a genuine zero. Present so that classifying a task is a decision with two directions, not a way to make numbers go up.

attestations.note: The stratified 10-task oracle probe. 10 runs, 4 excluded, 6 counted.

The 123-task scripted-agent measurement that produced the published chain-coverage figure. 123 runs discovered; 23 excluded, all 23 listed here and all 23 classified below with an `m1-` scope; 100 counted. `lean4-proof` is NOT excluded here — see its entry: the mechanism that excluded it from the probe is scoped to `probe-p1-` because the m1 shim provably never wrote the `pytest` wrapper the mechanism depends on. Excluding it anyway is how the published denominator became 99 instead of 100.

entries.mechanism: The PATH shim answers `command -v pytest`, so the task's setup skips `uv pip install pytest`; the real pytest is never installed and `run-tests.sh` dies at exit 127. The oracle's own solution was verified complete first, so a task the oracle SOLVES scores as a non-pass.
entries.evidence: runs-probe-p1-lean4-proof/probe-p1-lean4-proof/results.json -> is_resolved=null, failure_mode=parse_error; run_metadata.json -> accuracy=0.0, agent_name=oracle. mount-probe-p1-lean4-proof/READY present and spool/codex.jsonl non-empty, so this one reached `started` and lost only `graded`.
entries.scope_note: SCOPED TO THE PROBE ON PURPOSE. The shim's shadowing predicate was later amended to write a wrapper only where a real program of that name RESOLVES, and `mount-m1-lean4-proof/shim` holds exactly `make, python3, thruline-shim.json, uv, uvx` — no `pytest`. The m1 run of this task carries is_resolved=false, failure_mode=unset (a graded non-pass, not a parse error) and a complete capture. Carrying this entry unscoped removed a genuinely measured task from the m1 denominator on a mechanism that did not occur there, which is what made the published figure 64/99 rather than 65/100.

entries.mechanism: ThruLine's appended layer runs `if ! command -v git; then apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git; fi`. This task's own Dockerfile deliberately REPLACES /usr/bin/apt-get and /usr/bin/apt with a two-line stub that prints `E: Could not connect to archive.ubuntu.com` and exits 1 — that sabotage is the task. git is absent from the base, so ThruLine's layer runs the stub and the image never builds. Without ThruLine's layer the image builds; the damage is ours.

entries.mechanism: ThruLine's uv-provisioning layer ends with its own assertions `test -x $HOME/.local/bin/uv; test -f $HOME/.local/bin/env`. uv installs cleanly (the build log prints `installing to /root/.local/bin` and `everything's installed!`) but writes no `env` script, because this task's own Dockerfile already carries `ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:$PATH"`, so the installer sees its target directory on PATH and skips the shell-profile step. ThruLine's `test -f` then fails and the image never builds. Nothing but ThruLine's assertion failed.

entries.mechanism: The host `thruline` binary is bind-mounted read-only into the container at /usr/local/bin/thruline. It is `ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, ARM aarch64, dynamically linked, interpreter /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`. This task builds from `taichidev/taichi:v0.7.26`, which `docker image inspect` reports as `amd64/linux`, so the loader for that interpreter does not exist and the shell reports `thruline: not found`. The compose setup chain is one `&&` chain, so it stops at the `thruline hook-install` step: READY is never written, the container exits, and Terminal-Bench then reports `Recording is enabled but asciinema is not installed in the container` — the wrong subsystem entirely.
entries.evidence: mount-m1-accelerate-maximal-square/hook-install.log contains exactly `sh: 1: thruline: not found`; no shim-install.log, no READY, no exec.db, spool 0 bytes. runs-m1-accelerate-maximal-square/.../run.log -> RuntimeError asciinema. `file $PILOT/bin/thruline` -> ARM aarch64. `docker image inspect taichidev/taichi:v0.7.26 --format '{{.Architecture}}/{{.Os}}'` -> amd64/linux.

entries.mechanism: Same root cause as `accelerate-maximal-square`: the bind-mounted host `thruline` is an aarch64 ELF and this task's Dockerfile pins `FROM --platform=linux/amd64 ghcr.io/laude-institute/t-bench/python-3-13:20250620`, so the interpreter /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 is absent and `sh` reports `not found`. The setup chain stops at hook-install, the container exits, and Terminal-Bench misreports it as a missing asciinema.

entries.mechanism: The same root cause as the four `not found` tasks, wearing a different error string: the bind-mounted host `thruline` is dynamically linked against a newer glibc than the container has. This task builds `FROM debian:bullseye-slim` (glibc 2.31) and the loader resolves but the symbol versions do not. The setup chain stops at hook-install, the container exits, and docker reports 409 `container is not running`. Five m1 tasks share this one root cause and Terminal-Bench names two different wrong subsystems for it.

entries.mechanism: The image BUILDS and `docker compose up -d` succeeds; the container then exits before the setup chain finishes, and Terminal-Bench reports docker 409 `container is not running`. Neither /thruline/baseline-tree.txt nor /thruline/hook-install.log exists in the mount, and the compose chain redirects into both, so the chain died at or before `git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}'` — i.e. inside the profile.d/git-baseline prologue. WHICH of those nine steps failed is NOT established, and no container log survives. Recorded as argued rather than reproduced.

The mechanism changed under the file between the two runs, and nothing detected it — which is why entries now carry `applies_to`.

entries.mechanism: The compose file is correctly patched, the container ran, the agent ran, `run-tests.sh` executed and the task was graded — and the mount holds NONE of the setup chain's artefacts: no hook-install.log, no shim-install.log, no baseline-tree.txt, no READY, and a 0-byte spool. So the ThruLine setup chain produced nothing while the harness proceeded normally end to end. The cause is not established. This is the one exclusion in the m1 measurement recorded as argued in the report that produced it, and it stays argued here.
